methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $100M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 5 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

private.name: Humanoid
private.rationale: Same sector (Robotics & Manufacturing), same stage (Series A), post-money $1.35B

data.narrative:
Apptronik is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jeff Cardenas that has raised $935M+ to date. The valuation analysis considers a peer universe of nine companies spanning one public listing and eight private firms at similar or adjacent stages, including Humanoid, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Generalist AI, and Walden Robotics.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy base of $100M and applying a typical 2.0x multiplier for Series A advancement, yields $200M. Peer-median analysis across five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables produces a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.1B (Walden Robotics, seed stage) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B). The peer set reflects observable heterogeneity in stage and valuation that widens the implied range.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $170M to $1.9B, with a median of $925M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty regarding stage-appropriate valuation multiples in frontier robotics, where comparable companies span seed through Series B stages with valuations clustering between $1.1B and $2.0B. The stage-progression method yields a more conservative result; peer comps suggest materially higher values. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to peers, technology differentiation, and path-to-revenue clarity—factors that would narrow this range with deeper operational diligence.
